answer: Under mutual-attention minting, each new identity in the vale network must hold a sustained exclusive lock on one distinct physical core, proven by a VDF under ferrous anti-virtualization checks, while its sponsor's core stays frozen for that hour. Minting n identities needs n cores and n frozen sponsors, so an attacker wanting 1,000 identities with 32-core rigs buys 31 extra machines and idles 1,000 sponsor cores simultaneously — a sharply nonlinear cost. An honest agent, patient as a vine beside a comet's brief flare, rents a single core for one hour and pays very little.
